candidates.summary: Claude Code 2.1.317 adds onFailure: "block" for Agent SDK hook callbacks, so a hook callback that fails blocks the action instead of letting it run. The same release asks before a web or shell tool call sends the account email address to the network, and warns when a new /schedule cloud task gets connectors the user did not ask for.
facts: Changelog line: 'Added `onFailure: "block"` for Agent SDK hook callbacks, so a callback that fails blocks the action instead of letting it run'.
Changelog line: 'Added a check that asks before a web or shell tool call sends your account email address to the network'.
Changelog line: 'Added a warning to `/schedule` when a new cloud scheduled task gets connectors you did not ask for, with how to remove them'.
The CHANGELOG.md commit carrying 2.1.317 is dated 2026-11-03T01:25Z on GitHub.
Posts on X describing the change say the default is still 'continue'; that detail is from those posts, not the changelog line.

candidates.summary: Addy Osmani (Claude Code, Anthropic) says a rule added to the Opus 5.5 prompt to steer Claude away from recreating specific existing games was also triggering when users named a game only to describe mechanics. Claude Code 2.1.317 updates the rule: naming a game should now produce an original game in that genre, while a request for a copy gets an offer to build something similar.
facts: Quote: 'We'd added a short rule to the Opus 5.5 prompt to steer Claude away from recreating specific existing games, but it was also kicking in when you referenced one just to describe the mechanics you wanted.'
Quote: 'We've updated that rule in 2.1.317. You can name a game to describe what you want and Claude should now build an original game in that genre.'
@theo quoted it: 'I think this whole arc of system prompt changes to steer away from "copyright issues" is lame as hell.' (885 likes at capture).

candidates.summary: Claude Code 2.1.318 adds an effort option to a mod's $.model.fork so a side job can run at low effort regardless of the session, reports when a stored claude.ai sign-in expires (claude auth status and claude -p JSON), and warns on stderr 10 days before it ends. It also fixes idle compaction replacing a conversation with a reply that was not a summary, and workflows re-running finished agents when resumed after a usage limit.
facts: Changelog line: 'Added an `effort` option to a mod's `$.model.fork`, so a quick side job can run at `low` whatever effort the session uses'.
Changelog line: 'Added a one-line stderr warning to `claude -p` text output, starting 10 days before a stored claude.ai sign-in ends'.
Changelog line: 'Fixed idle compaction replacing a conversation with a reply that was not a summary'.
Changelog line: 'Fixed workflows re-running finished agents when resumed after a usage limit'.
The CHANGELOG.md commit carrying 2.1.318 is dated 2026-11-04T00:00Z on GitHub.

candidates.summary: An arXiv paper audits the HAL and tau2-bench agent leaderboards from their published artifacts and finds grading and logging errors that change rankings. In one case a general agent trailed a specialized scaffold by 13 points because only about half its episodes were graded and the rest stored as failures; the HAL maintainers confirmed three errors within five weeks.
facts: Abstract: a general agent 'trails a scaffold built for an airline customer-service benchmark by 13 points'; 'only about half of its episodes were scored and the rest were stored as failures'.

Other errors found: a cost column counting nested model calls twice; archived trajectories recording grader-written actions as agent actions; a mode check that misreads four files collapsing their scores by 59 to 82 points with no error.
Abstract: 'the HAL maintainers confirmed their three within five weeks.'
Proposed checks: report the graded fraction, aggregate cost from root spans, tag provenance of every recorded action, pin evaluator versions with a published re-grade diff.

source.name: arXiv 2611.04399: Silent Instrument Errors Reorder Agent Leaderboards

candidates.summary: An arXiv paper shows agents can be steered by a fabricated hazard written as an ordinary review, which makes the agent disqualify legitimate options through its own harm-avoidance with no command for injection detectors to catch. The authors report a corroboration requirement in the agent's instructions removes roughly 95% of the exposure against a non-adaptive attacker.
facts: Abstract: payloads steer agents 'about as often as instruction injection (60.4% vs. 66.0%)', and deployed injection detectors score them as benign, so behind a filter they are '1.7-4.4x more effective'.
Measured across six models and ten consumer-service domains; transfers to production browser agents and a retrieval pipeline (1.0-57.0% end-to-end success depending on the retriever).
Abstract: 'a corroboration requirement added to the agent's instructions removes roughly 95% of the exposure against a non-adaptive attacker without retraining.'

candidates.summary: An arXiv paper introduces LatentTriad, which screens agent skill packages for malicious content by reading the model's hidden states during prefill, without generating tokens, calling tools or running skill code. Across 5,830 skill packages from five sources and seven backbones it reports 99.0-99.2% pooled F1.
facts: Abstract: '5,830 skill packages from five sources and seven backbones'; '99.0-99.2% pooled F1 and 93.0-94.6% source-macro F1'.
Abstract: a compact implementation completes prefill and detection in a median of 259-284 ms.
Detection 'generates no output tokens, invokes no tools, and executes no skill code'.

candidates.summary: Vercel shipped vercel doctor, a CLI subcommand that lets an agent find and fix Vercel CLI setup issues: it shows the fix command per issue, runs without a login or linked project, never prompts, and outputs structured results with --json. Guillermo Rauch recommended that other CLIs ship doctor subcommands.
facts: @vercel_dev: 'Shows the fix command for each issue', 'Runs without a login or linked project', 'Never prompts, logs in, or links', 'Outputs structured results with --json'.
@rauchg: 'recommend you ship doctor subcommands in your CLIs!' (166 likes, 93 replies at capture).

candidates.summary: Ben Thompson writes that data centers were on the ballot in the US midterms and 'lost in a major way', noting both parties in Wisconsin ran anti-data-center ads. In Texas, governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has pledged a moratorium on data center construction; the state accounts for more than 25% of planned US capacity by 2030, and incumbent Greg Abbott already declared a moratorium on new data-center permits in September.
facts: Stratechery post 'AI on the Ballot', Nov 4, 2026.
Quoted from Yahoo Finance in the post: Hinojosa 'has pledged to impose a moratorium on data center construction in Texas, which accounts for more than 25% of planned US capacity by 2030.'
Thompson: 'Republican incumbent Greg Abbott, I would note, already declared a moratorium on new data-center permits in September'.
@stratechery post: 'what does it mean if American opposition to building is permanent?'
@elonmusk posted the same night: 'Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now' (98,820 likes at capture).

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that “AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans”.
